doc.title: Arturo Sandoval interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 12, 2023

chapter: Career, recognition and jazz in America
title: Music saved my life: poor Cuban countryside boyhood
summary: Sandoval says music changed his life from a hopeless, poor country childhood in Cuba and let him support his family and see the world.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Excellent. So are you a man who likes down time? I know that’s kind of a strange question but I get the sense that your head is constantly filled with music.
You know what I always say, music saved my life. Music saved my life. And I owe everything to the music.
Well that sums it up then.

Yeah and then it’s my — I mean my appreciation toward the music because when I was young man I grew up in the middle of nowhere of the countryside of the island of Cuba. My family was really poor. And I really was a kind of a hopeless kid. And then because of music my life changed completely and you know I’ve been blessed because of the music I traveled all over the world and I’ve been able to give a decent life to my family and raise my kid and now my son is doing great, he’s very successful, he’s very happy about his career and what he’s doing. He’s a graphic artist. And you know I have a lot of reason to be grateful to the music.
